```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("R/simulate_bdat602_data.R")
health_small <- simulate_bdat602(n = 10000, seed = 602)
```

## Task 1 — Count NAs

```{r task1}
colSums(is.na(health_small[, c("bmi", "income", "complaint_notes")]))
```

`bmi` has ~500 NAs (5%), `income` ~400 (4%), `complaint_notes` ~1,000 (10%).

## Task 2 — Median imputation with indicator

```{r task2}
library(dplyr)

bmi_median  <- median(health_small$bmi, na.rm = TRUE)
health_clean <- health_small |>
  mutate(
    bmi_missing = as.integer(is.na(bmi)),
    bmi         = if_else(is.na(bmi), bmi_median, bmi)
  )

colSums(is.na(health_clean[, c("bmi", "bmi_missing")]))
```

`bmi` now has 0 NAs. `bmi_missing` has no NAs (it is a computed integer column).

## Task 3 — recipes imputation

```{r task3}
library(recipes)

impute_rec  <- recipe(claim_amount ~ ., data = health_small) |>
  step_impute_median(income)

impute_prep <- prep(impute_rec, training = health_small)
health_imp  <- bake(impute_prep, new_data = health_small)

sum(is.na(health_imp$income))
```

After baking, `income` has **0** missing values. The median was learned from the training data in `prep()` and applied in `bake()` — no leakage.
